entries.symptom: PowerShell aborts before the installer can fetch or report a failure.
entries.root_cause: A colon immediately followed the interpolated $LASTEXITCODE variable.
entries.guard: Brace LASTEXITCODE when it is followed by a colon.

entries.symptom: A helper or binary fetch can fail and leave an unexplained installer error.
entries.root_cause: Network failures must be converted into a diagnostic and the staging file must be removed.
entries.guard: Invoke-WebRequest uses ErrorAction Stop inside catch blocks; failed downloads clean staging files.

entries.symptom: macOS/Linux installer exits from the raw curl/wget fetch, without a useful error or cleanup.
entries.root_cause: The staged binary fetch was called directly while install.sh uses set -e.
entries.guard: The staged asset fetch is wrapped, reports the URL, and removes the temporary file before exit.

entries.symptom: A valid login is reported as inactive when the account email is returned under user.email.
entries.root_cause: Installers only inspected identity.email during a staged auth schema transition.
entries.guard: Both installers accept identity.email and the legacy user.email shape.

entries.symptom: Customers copy an obsolete channel or cannot run the installed CLI in the current terminal.
entries.root_cause: Public docs mixed install channels and did not make the session-only PATH step explicit.
entries.guard: Docs use the canonical master installer URLs, explain current-session PATH, and point to the managed binary.

entries.symptom: Bootstrap contract tests still expect the old require_active_login/verify_mcp_tools ordering.
entries.root_cause: Installer behavior moved to report_login_state plus direct MCP registration, but the old tests were not reconciled.
entries.guard: Keep the failing tests as a release sentinel until the intended login/MCP contract is decided and implemented.
entries.next_action: Reconcile the test contract with the intended fail-closed MCP behavior.

entries.symptom: Codex integration test rejects the current mutable-master hook reference policy.
entries.root_cause: The test and installer policy disagree on the allowed opt-in hook reference.
entries.guard: Keep the sentinel until the hook ref policy is made explicit and both code and test agree.
entries.next_action: Choose a version-pinned hook policy and update the contract.

entries.symptom: Uninstall/rollback contract tests expect transaction markers and purge semantics absent from the current scripts.
entries.root_cause: The installer implementation and the transaction test contract have drifted.
entries.guard: Keep all three failing sentinels recorded; do not silently weaken purge or rollback expectations.
entries.next_action: Reconcile the desired uninstall contract before changing deletion behavior.

entries.symptom: The macOS Intel contract test still demands the obsolete macos-x86_64 manifest alias.
entries.root_cause: The test expects a naming convention different from distribution/targets.json and the published manifest, which use macos-x64.
entries.guard: Keep the sentinel until the canonical target naming decision is recorded and the test is corrected.
entries.next_action: Confirm whether macos-x64 is canonical; then update the stale test or the distribution table.

entries.symptom: The benchmark audit timing/CLI report test is not deterministic in the current environment.
entries.root_cause: The test combines measured timing with a strict report assertion.
entries.guard: Keep the failure visible as a quality-gate sentinel rather than hiding it behind a skip.
entries.next_action: Separate timing tolerance from report-file correctness.

entries.symptom: The PyPI installer test finds a default manifest pin that does not match the versioned checkout.
entries.root_cause: The wrapper's default source/version pin drifted from the public release metadata.
entries.guard: Keep the packaging sentinel active until the wrapper and checkout provenance are aligned.
entries.next_action: Align the PyPI default pin with the versioned public checkout and release manifest.
